newsitem.title: USA: Peregrine in pact to buy four GM plants.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine in pact to buy four GM plants.

text.p: Peregrine Inc said Monday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire four component parts plants from General Motors Corp.
The four plants collectively will generate 1996 sales to GM's North American operations of more than $1 billion, Peregrine said.
The transaction is expected to close by the end of the year.

The four GM plants are in Flint and Livonia, Mich., and Windsor and Oshawa, Ontario. Products include window regulators, door hardware, interior trim, structural plastics, and metal stampings, Peregrine said.
Edward Gulda, Peregrine's chairman and chief executive, said a management team is already in place and is implementing an aggressive, growth-oriented plan.

"We look forward to continuing discussions with the people at each of the plants and to working with this fine group," Gulda said. "We are confident that Peregrine will be a strong competitor in North America and worldwide and that we can work toward a bright future together."
Peregrine is a company formed by the investment firm Joseph Littlejohn & Levy and Gulda, an automotive executive.
